claim: Ammonium serves as a key nitrogen source and metabolic intermediate.
source: Ammonium serves as key nitrogen source and metabolic intermediate, yet excess causes toxicity.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about ammonium's biological role.

claim: Excess ammonium causes toxicity.
source: Ammonium serves as key nitrogen source and metabolic intermediate, yet excess causes toxicity.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about ammonium toxicity.

claim: Ammonium uptake is mediated by ammonium transporters.
source: Ammonium uptake is mediated by ammonium transporters, whose regulation is poorly understood.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about ammonium transport mechanisms.

claim: The regulation of ammonium transporters is poorly understood.
source: Ammonium uptake is mediated by ammonium transporters, whose regulation is poorly understood.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: Transport can easily be characterized in heterologous systems.
source: While transport can easily be characterized in heterologous systems, measuring transporter activity in vivo remains challenging.
evidence: This is established knowledge about experimental methods in the field.

claim: Measuring transporter activity in vivo remains challenging.
source: While transport can easily be characterized in heterologous systems, measuring transporter activity in vivo remains challenging.
evidence: This is a statement about current limitations in the field.

claim: A simple assay for monitoring ammonium transceptor activity in vivo was developed by inserting circularly-permutated GFP into conformation-sensitive positions.
source: Here we developed a simple assay for monitoring activity in vivo by inserting circularly-permutated GFP into conformation-sensitive positions of two plant and one yeast ammonium transceptors ('AmTrac' and 'MepTrac').
evidence: This is the primary finding of the study, supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: Addition of ammonium to yeast cells expressing the sensors triggered concentration-dependent fluorescence intensity changes.
source: Addition of ammonium to yeast cells expressing the sensors triggered concentration-dependent fluorescence intensity (FI) changes that strictly correlated with the activity of the transporter.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in multiple figures (e.g., Figure 4C, Figure 5D).

claim: The fluorescence intensity changes strictly correlated with the activity of the transporter.
source: Addition of ammonium to yeast cells expressing the sensors triggered concentration-dependent fluorescence intensity (FI) changes that strictly correlated with the activity of the transporter.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing correlation between transport activity and fluorescence response (e.g., Figure 7E).

claim: Fluorescence-based activity sensors present a novel technology for monitoring the interaction of transporters with their substrates.
source: Fluorescence-based activity sensors present a novel technology for monitoring the interaction of the transporters with their substrates, the activity of transporters and their regulation in vivo, which is particularly valuable in the context of analytes for which no radiotracers exist, as well as for cell-specific and subcellular transport processes that are otherwise difficult to track.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results presented in the study.

claim: Patch clamping has largely been limited to the analysis of processes at the cell membrane, or cells at the surface of sliced tissues.
source: However, patch clamping has largely been limited to the analysis of processes at the cell membrane, or cells at the surface of sliced tissues.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the limitations of patch clamp techniques.

claim: Fluorescent proteins enable observation of cellular processes in living cells of intact tissues.
source: A new level of insight was provided by fluorescent proteins enabling us to observe cellular processes in living cells of intact tissues (Tsien, 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Tsien, 2006.

claim: FRET sensors have allowed monitoring of analyte levels and dynamics in live cells with minimal invasive methods.
source: Fluorescence Resonance Energy Transfer (FRET) sensors have allowed us to monitor analyte levels and dynamics in live cells with minimal invasive methods (Okumoto et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Okumoto et al., 2012.

claim: It has not been possible to directly follow the activity of transporters and to monitor their regulation in vivo prior to this work.
source: Yet to date, we have not been able to directly follow the activity of transporters and to monitor their regulation in vivo.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of the field before this study.

claim: Circularly-permutated versions of GFP have successfully been used to monitor structural rearrangements of calmodulin.
source: Circularly-permutated versions of GFP (cpGFP) have successfully been used to monitor structural rearrangements of calmodulin (Baird et al., 1999; Nagai et al., 2001; Nakai et al., 2001; Wang et al., 2008; Akerboom et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous work.

claim: Ammonium transport is key to nitrogen nutrition of bacteria, fungi and plants.
source: Ammonium transport is key to nitrogen nutrition of bacteria, fungi and plants.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about ammonium's role in biology.

claim: Ammonium transporters play key roles in renal ammonium secretion and male fertility in mammals.
source: Although mammals are unable to assimilate ammonium into amino acids, ammonium transporters play key roles in renal ammonium secretion and male fertility (Biver et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Biver et al., 2008.

claim: Ammonium transport is electrogenic.
source: Ammonium transport is electrogenic and is mediated by high affinity ammonium transporters of the AMT/MEP/Rhesus protein superfamily (Marini et al., 1994; Ninnemann et al., 1994; Tremblay and Hallenbeck, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The genome of Arabidopsis contains six AMT paralogs.
source: The genome of the plant Arabidopsis contains six AMT paralogs, four of which (AMT1;1, 1;2, 1;3, and 1;5) are partially redundant and together essential for ammonium acquisition (Yuan et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Yuan et al., 2007.

claim: Four AMT paralogs (AMT1;1, 1;2, 1;3, and 1;5) are partially redundant and together essential for ammonium acquisition in Arabidopsis.
source: The genome of the plant Arabidopsis contains six AMT paralogs, four of which (AMT1;1, 1;2, 1;3, and 1;5) are partially redundant and together essential for ammonium acquisition (Yuan et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Yuan et al., 2007.

claim: Ammonium acquisition in plants is highly regulated and is subject to feedback inhibition.
source: In plants, ammonium acquisition is highly regulated and is subject to feedback inhibition, potentially as a means of preventing accumulation of ammonium to toxic levels (Wang et al., 1993; Kronzucker et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Wang et al., 1993 and Kronzucker et al., 2001.

claim: Ammonium-triggered phosphorylation of a critical threonine in the cytosolic C-terminus of AMT1;1 leads to inhibition of ammonium transport by allosteric regulation in the trimeric transporter complex.
source: Recent results show that ammonium-triggered phosphorylation of a critical threonine in the cytosolic C-terminus of AMT1;1 leads to inhibition of ammonium transport by allosteric regulation in the trimeric transporter complex (Loqué et al., 2007; Lanquar et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Loqué et al., 2007 and Lanquar et al., 2009.

claim: AMT1;3 functions as an electrogenic high-affinity ammonium transporter involved in nitrogen uptake in Arabidopsis roots.
source: The close homolog AMT1;3, also functions as an electrogenic high-affinity ammonium transporter involved in nitrogen uptake in Arabidopsis roots (Gazzarrini et al., 1999).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Gazzarrini et al., 1999.

claim: AMT1;3 functions in homo- and hetero-trimeric complexes with AMT1;1 and is allosterically regulated.
source: AMT1;3 functions in homo- and hetero-trimeric complexes with the coexpressed AMT1;1 and is allosterically regulated (Yuan et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Yuan et al., 2013.

claim: AMT1;3 not only functions as a transporter, but in addition controls root architecture.
source: AMT1;3 not only functions as a transporter, but in addition controls root architecture by a process similar to the one found for the yeast MEP2 transceptor (dual function transporter and receptor), a protein that mediates ammonium transport and regulates pseudohyphal growth (Boeckstaens et al., 2007; Lima et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Boeckstaens et al., 2007 and Lima et al., 2010.

claim: Yeast MEP2 is a transceptor that mediates ammonium transport and regulates pseudohyphal growth.
source: AMT1;3 not only functions as a transporter, but in addition controls root architecture by a process similar to the one found for the yeast MEP2 transceptor (dual function transporter and receptor), a protein that mediates ammonium transport and regulates pseudohyphal growth (Boeckstaens et al., 2007; Lima et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Boeckstaens et al., 2007 and Lima et al., 2010.

claim: AMT1;3 activity was extremely sensitive to manipulation of loops 7–8 and 9–10 or the cytosolic C-terminus.
source: AMT1;3 activity was extremely sensitive to manipulation of loops 7–8 and 9–10 or the cytosolic C-terminus (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Modification of loop 5–6 (L5–6, position K233) by insertion of either two amino acid residues or mcpGFP was tolerated.
source: However, modification of loop 5–6 (L5–6, position K233) by insertion of either two amino acid residues (encoded as part of the restriction site XbaI) or mcpGFP was tolerated (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: mTFP or Venus insertions inhibited transport activity.
source: In contrast, mTFP or Venus insertions inhibited transport activity.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: L5–6 is located between the two pseudo-symmetric halves of the protein and connects two transmembrane helices (TMH-V and -VI) that contain residues postulated to be directly involved in recruitment, gating and substrate translocation.
source: Interestingly, L5–6 is located between the two pseudo-symmetric halves of the protein and connects two transmembrane helices (TMH-V and -VI) that contain residues postulated to be directly involved in recruitment, gating and substrate translocation (Figure 1C; Andrade et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Andrade et al., 2005 and structural information shown in Figure 1C.

claim: TMH-V has been proposed to oscillate during substrate transport.
source: Moreover, TMH-V has been proposed to oscillate during substrate transport (Andrade et al., 2005; Inwood et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Andrade et al., 2005 and Inwood et al., 2009.

claim: Addition of ammonium to yeast cells expressing the AMT1;3-mcpGFP fusion did not lead to detectable changes in fluorescence intensity.
source: In initial tests, addition of ammonium to yeast cells expressing the AMT1;3-mcpGFP fusion did not lead to detectable changes in fluorescence intensity (FI; data not shown).
evidence: This is an experimental observation reported by the authors.

claim: cpGFP-based sensors for calcium and maltose are exquisitely sensitive to modifications in the linker sequences.
source: However, it is known that the cpGFP-based sensors for calcium and maltose are exquisitely sensitive to modifications in the linker sequences connecting to the respective binding proteins (Wang et al., 2008; Akerboom et al., 2009; Marvin et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Wang et al., 2008, Akerboom et al., 2009, and Marvin et al., 2011.

claim: All 24 linker variants maintained transport activity.
source: All 24 variants maintained transport activity (Figure 2A); importantly some variants showed a FI response to addition of 1 mM NH4Cl (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Some linker variants showed a FI response to addition of 1 mM NH4Cl.
source: All 24 variants maintained transport activity (Figure 2A); importantly some variants showed a FI response to addition of 1 mM NH4Cl (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The variant showing the strongest response (40% FI change) was named AmTrac.
source: The variant showing the strongest response (40% FI change) was named AmTrac (Ammonium Transporter coupled to mcpGFP).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: In AmTrac, mcpGFP had been inserted into position 233 of AMT1;3, centrally located in the cytosolic loop L5–6 and flanked via linker sequences containing Leu-Glu and Phe-Asn at the N- and C-terminus, respectively.
source: In AmTrac, mcpGFP had been inserted into position 233 of AMT1;3, centrally located in the cytosolic loop L5–6 and flanked via linker sequences containing Leu-Glu and Phe-Asn at the N- and C-terminus, respectively (Figure 2C,D).
evidence: This is a description of the AmTrac construct, supported by Figure 2C,D.

claim: Both transport activity and fluorescence response were highest in variants with mcpGFP inserted in central positions of L5–6.
source: Both transport activity and fluorescence response were highest in variants with mcpGFP inserted in central positions of L5–6, with a clear correlation between activity and FI change (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: There is a clear correlation between transport activity and FI change.
source: Both transport activity and fluorescence response were highest in variants with mcpGFP inserted in central positions of L5–6, with a clear correlation between activity and FI change (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Loop length is critical for AmTrac function.
source: Loop length also proved to be critical. In variants with incremental deletions in the middle of L5–6 around the insertion point of mcpGFP, deletion of four or more residues abolished transport activity and the fluorescence response (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Deletion of four or more residues in L5–6 abolished transport activity and the fluorescence response.
source: In variants with incremental deletions in the middle of L5–6 around the insertion point of mcpGFP, deletion of four or more residues abolished transport activity and the fluorescence response (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: All variants that responded to ammonium with a FI change were functional transporters.
source: Importantly, all variants that responded to ammonium with a FI change were functional transporters, indicating that AmTrac reports transport activity.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: The FI response of AmTrac was proportional to the ammonium concentration added to the yeast cells.
source: Initial experiments showed that the FI response of AmTrac was proportional to the ammonium concentration added to the yeast cells (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The mcpGFP insertion into AMT1;3 did not significantly affect the affinity constant for ammonium transport (Km ∼ 50 µM) when tested in Xenopus oocytes using two-electrode voltage clamp analysis.
source: The mcpGFP insertion into AMT1;3 did not significantly affect the affinity constant for ammonium transport (Km ∼ 50 µM) when tested in Xenopus oocytes using two-electrode voltage clamp (TEVC) analysis (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The affinity constant for the FI response of AmTrac to NH4Cl (EC50 55 ± 7 µM) is strikingly similar to the transport kinetics of AMT1;3 measured in oocytes and in Arabidopsis roots (Km 57 µM).
source: Notably, the affinity constant for the FI response of AmTrac to NH4Cl (EC50 55 ± 7 µM) is strikingly similar to that reported here in oocytes and to the reported transport kinetics of AMT1;3 as measured in roots of Arabidopsis plants expressing only AMT1;3 (Km 57 µM; Figure 4C; Yuan et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C and citation to Yuan et al., 2007.

claim: AmTrac responses were detectable in single cells, were concentration-dependent, and were readily reversible.
source: AmTrac responses were detectable in single cells, were concentration-dependent, and were readily reversible, demonstrating that AmTrac can be used in vivo to quantify ammonium transport activity and to observe kinetics of the chimeric transporter in response to substrate availability (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The unique selectivity of AMT1 for ammonium over potassium was retained for FI responses.
source: The unique selectivity of AMT1 for ammonium over potassium was retained for FI responses (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Other cations did not induce a change in FI.
source: Also other cations did not induce a change in FI.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: NH4NO3 and (NH4)2SO4 elicited the same FI change as NH4Cl.
source: NH4NO3 and (NH4)2SO4 elicited the same FI change as NH4Cl, demonstrating that chloride does not affect the FI response.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Chloride does not affect the FI response.
source: NH4NO3 and (NH4)2SO4 elicited the same FI change as NH4Cl, demonstrating that chloride does not affect the FI response.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that different ammonium salts produce the same response.

claim: Addition of equimolar concentrations of sodium, potassium, calcium, magnesium, manganese or zinc did not trigger a change in FI.
source: Furthermore, addition of equimolar concentrations of sodium, potassium, calcium, magnesium, manganese or zinc did not trigger a change in FI (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: The majority of the brightest variants carried a Ser residue instead of a Glu in the position immediately preceding the mcpGFP insertion.
source: Interestingly, the majority of the brightest variants carried a Ser residue instead of a Glu in the position immediately preceding the mcpGFP insertion (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: AmTrac-LS was as responsive to ammonium as AmTrac (∼40% FI change), but was approximately fivefold brighter.
source: AmTrac-LS, a sensor with a Leu-Ser linker, was as responsive to ammonium as AmTrac (∼40% FI change), but was approximately fivefold brighter (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The excitation spectra of AmTrac-LS revealed two maxima, a minor peak of the protonated chromophore at λex ∼ 380 nm and a major peak of the deprotonated chromophore at λex ∼ 495 nm.
source: The excitation spectra revealed two maxima, a minor peak of the protonated chromophore at λex ∼ 380 nm and a major peak of the deprotonated chromophore at λex ∼ 495 nm.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: For the emission spectra one maximum was detected at λem ∼ 513 nm.
source: For the emission spectra one maximum was detected at λem ∼ 513 nm (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: No shifts in the fluorescence maxima were observed when ammonium was added.
source: No shifts in the fluorescence maxima were observed, while FI decreased by 30–40% in a concentration-dependent manner when ammonium was added .
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: FI decreased by 30–40% in a concentration-dependent manner when ammonium was added.
source: No shifts in the fluorescence maxima were observed, while FI decreased by 30–40% in a concentration-dependent manner when ammonium was added .
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The linker modifications had no significant effect on the transport kinetics.
source: The linker modifications had no significant effect on the transport kinetics (tested for AmTrac-LS; Figure 4B), nor on the EC50 of the fluorescence response (shown for AmTrac-IS, Ile-Ser linker; Figure 5D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B and Figure 5D.

claim: AmTrac-LS responses showed reversibility of the FI change when ammonium was removed.
source: AmTrac-LS responses were monitored in single yeast cells as described above and also showed reversibility of the FI change when ammonium was removed (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: Mutations D202N, G460D, and T464D known to inactivate AMT1 transporters abolished both transport activity and fluorescence response when introduced into AmTrac.
source: To further corroborate the correlation between transport activity and ammonium-induced FI change, mutations (D202N, G460D, T464D) known to inactivate AMT1 transporters were introduced into AmTrac (Loqué et al., 2007; Neuhäuser et al., 2007). While these mutations did not affect plasma membrane localization of AmTrac (Figure 6A), both transport activity and fluorescence response were abolished (Figure 6B,C), indicating that transport activity is tightly correlated with the FI response of AmTrac.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A, 6B, and 6C, and citations to Loqué et al., 2007 and Neuhäuser et al., 2007.

claim: These mutations did not affect plasma membrane localization of AmTrac.
source: While these mutations did not affect plasma membrane localization of AmTrac (Figure 6A), both transport activity and fluorescence response were abolished (Figure 6B,C), indicating that transport activity is tightly correlated with the FI response of AmTrac.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: None of the transport-deficient AmTrac versions produced an FI response when expressed in wild type yeast carrying endogenous ammonium transporters.
source: In the presence of an independent set of functional ammonium transporters, none of the transport-deficient AmTrac versions produced an FI response (Figure 6D), providing strong evidence that cytosolic ammonium accumulation did not elicit the FI response.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Cytosolic ammonium accumulation did not elicit the FI response.
source: In the presence of an independent set of functional ammonium transporters, none of the transport-deficient AmTrac versions produced an FI response (Figure 6D), providing strong evidence that cytosolic ammonium accumulation did not elicit the FI response.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that transport-deficient variants do not respond even when intracellular ammonium is present due to endogenous transporters.

claim: Generation of intracellular ammonium from arginine catabolism failed to trigger an AmTrac response.
source: As a further test, generation of intracellular ammonium from arginine catabolism (Marini et al., 1997) failed to trigger an AmTrac response (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6E and citation to Marini et al., 1997.

claim: AmTrac responds to extracellular and not intracellular ammonium levels.
source: Taken together, these results indicate that AmTrac responds to extracellular and not intracellular ammonium levels.
evidence: This is inferred from the experiments showing that intracellular ammonium does not trigger a response.

claim: A saturating multicopy suppressor screen with the inactive mutant AmTrac-T464D identified eight gain-of-function mutations.
source: A saturating multicopy suppressor screen with the inactive mutant AmTrac-T464D (analogous to T460D in AMT1;1) (Loqué et al., 2007) identified eight gain-of-function mutations (Figure 7A and Table 1), seven in the pore region and one pseudo-reversion, D464V (Figure 7B–D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7A and Table 1, and citation to Loqué et al., 2007.

claim: Seven suppressor mutations were in the pore region and one was a pseudo-reversion, D464V.
source: A saturating multicopy suppressor screen with the inactive mutant AmTrac-T464D (analogous to T460D in AMT1;1) (Loqué et al., 2007) identified eight gain-of-function mutations (Figure 7A and Table 1), seven in the pore region and one pseudo-reversion, D464V (Figure 7B–D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7A, Table 1, and Figure 7B-D.

claim: The extent to which the suppressors were able to restore transport activity was highly correlated with the FI response (R2=0.72).
source: The extent to which the suppressors were able to restore transport activity, as measured by growth, was highly correlated with the FI response (R2=0.72; Figure 7E,F), further supporting the tight link between transport activity and FI response.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7E and 7F.

claim: One of the suppressor mutants, AmTrac-T464D-A141E, mediated hypersensitivity to elevated ammonium concentrations.
source: Interestingly, one of the suppressor mutants, AmTrac-T464D-A141E, mediated hypersensitivity to elevated ammonium concentrations (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: AmTrac-T464D-A141E functions as a low affinity/ high capacity ammonium transporter with a Km ∼ 3.5 mM.
source: TEVC analysis demonstrates that AmTrac-T464D-A141E functions as a low affinity/ high capacity ammonium transporter with a Km ∼ 3.5 mM (Figure 8A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: The fluorescence response of AmTrac-T464D-A141E (AmTrac-100µ) increased (EC50 = 101 ± 10 µM).
source: The fluorescence response of AmTrac-T464D-A141E (AmTrac-100µ) also increased (EC50 = 101 ± 10 µM; Figure 8B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8B.

claim: Insertion of mcpGFP in the center of L5–6 of both AMT1;2 and MEP2 with the same linkers as in AmTrac-LS generated two functional sensors (named AmTrac1;2 and MepTrac) that maintained transport activity.
source: Notwithstanding, insertion of mcpGFP in the center of L5–6 of both AMT1;2 and MEP2 (after amino acids R242 and R217, respectively) with the same linkers as in AmTrac-LS, generated two functional sensors (named AmTrac1;2 and MepTrac) that maintained transport activity (Figure 9A) and responded to ammonium addition with a fluorescence change (Figure 9B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 9A and 9B.

claim: AmTrac1;2 and MepTrac responded to ammonium addition with a fluorescence change.
source: Notwithstanding, insertion of mcpGFP in the center of L5–6 of both AMT1;2 and MEP2 (after amino acids R242 and R217, respectively) with the same linkers as in AmTrac-LS, generated two functional sensors (named AmTrac1;2 and MepTrac) that maintained transport activity (Figure 9A) and responded to ammonium addition with a fluorescence change (Figure 9B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 9B.

claim: The original MepTrac showed only a low response when tested at pH 6.
source: The original MepTrac showed only a low response when tested at pH 6.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 9B.

claim: MEP2 has a pH optimum at low pH.
source: In contrast to AMTs, MEP2 has a pH optimum at low pH.
evidence: This is established knowledge about MEP2 properties.

claim: Histidine-194 in the pore of MEP2 has been shown to be responsible for the lower pH optimum.
source: Histidine-194 in the pore of MEP2 has been shown to be responsible for the lower pH optimum (Boeckstaens et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Boeckstaens et al., 2008.

claim: A variant of MepTrac carrying the H194E mutation showed a significantly increased FI response.
source: A variant of MepTrac carrying the H194E mutation showed a significantly increased FI response, in agreement with the broader pH optimum conferred by this mutation (Boeckstaens et al., 2008; Figure 9B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 9B and citation to Boeckstaens et al., 2008.

claim: The response of AmTrac1;2, MepTrac and MepTrac-H194E to ammonium addition were dose-dependent.
source: Similar to AmTrac, the response of AmTrac1;2, MepTrac and MepTrac-H194E to ammonium addition were dose-dependent.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 9B.

claim: The AmTrac1;2 and MepTrac sensors were generated in a single step by using the linker and position information acquired during AmTrac development.
source: It is noteworthy that the AmTrac1;2 and MepTrac sensors were generated in a single step by using the linker and position information acquired during AmTrac development.
evidence: This is a statement about the methodology used to create these sensors.

claim: Crystal structures of AMTs from E. coli and A. fulgidus did not reveal obvious conformational differences when generated in the presence or absence of ammonium.
source: Crystal structures of AMTs from Escherichia coli (Khademi et al., 2004; Zheng et al., 2004) and Archaeoglobus fulgidus (Andrade et al., 2005) did not reveal obvious conformational differences when generated in the presence or absence of ammonium; observations that led to the proposition that AMTs are rigid gas channels (Khademi et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Khademi et al., 2004, Zheng et al., 2004, and Andrade et al., 2005.

claim: Electrophysiological studies challenged the hypothesis that AMTs transport the uncharged form ammonia by demonstrating that plant AMTs are electrogenic and show minimal or no ammonia conductivity.
source: Electrophysiological studies challenged the hypothesis that AMTs transport the uncharged form ammonia by demonstrating that plant AMTs are electrogenic and show minimal or no ammonia conductivity (Mayer et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Mayer et al., 2006.

claim: Mutations in the pore release the transporter from a gating control, leading to massively increased transport capacity and an up to 100-fold increase in the Km.
source: The transport of the charged form of ammonium is further supported by the finding that mutations in the pore release the transporter from a gating control, leading to massively increased transport capacity and an up to 100-fold increase in the Km (Figure 8A; Loqué et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8A and citation to Loqué et al., 2009.

claim: The fluorescence response of AmTrac variants and MepTrac supports the hypothesis that AMT1;3, AMT1;2 and MEP2 undergo conformational changes during transport.
source: The fluorescence response of AmTrac variants and MepTrac supports the hypothesis that AMT1;3, AMT1;2 and MEP2 undergo conformational changes during transport.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental observations of fluorescence changes during transport.

claim: The results are consistent with the hypothesis that TMH-V and -VI of AMT move relative to each other as a result of ammonium binding or during ammonium translocation.
source: Our results are consistent with the hypothesis that TMH-V and -VI of AMT move relative to each other as a result of ammonium binding or during ammonium translocation, thus affecting the conformation of L5–6 and thereby gating the inserted mcpGFP.
evidence: This is a hypothesis inferred from the experimental results.

claim: The pseudo-symmetry of AMTs with an inverted repeat of a five TMH containing domain is comparable to that found in the LeuT transporter.
source: Interestingly, the pseudo-symmetry of AMTs with an inverted repeat of a five TMH containing domain is comparable to that found in the LeuT transporter (Krishnamurthy and Gouaux, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Krishnamurthy and Gouaux, 2012.

claim: LeuT carries a substrate-binding site at the interface of the two repeats and undergoes a transport cycle for which multiple states have been identified.
source: LeuT carries a substrate-binding site at the interface of the two repeats and undergoes a transport cycle for which multiple states have been identified (Forrest and Rudnick, 2009; Rudnick, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Forrest and Rudnick, 2009 and Rudnick, 2011.

claim: The transport pore of the AMTs is located between the two pseudo-symmetric halves, with TMH-V and -VI carrying key residues for ammonium translocation.
source: Similarly, the transport pore of the AMTs is located between the two pseudo-symmetric halves, with TMH-V and -VI (connected by L5–6) carrying key residues for ammonium translocation.
evidence: This is based on structural knowledge and previous studies.

claim: The data are consistent with the occurrence of structural rearrangements during transport.
source: Our data are consistent with the occurrence of structural rearrangements during transport; crystal structures for different states will be required to determine the conformational state during transport.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental observations.

claim: The combination of two ammonium transport activity sensors from different organisms will be useful for dissecting endogenous control mechanisms.
source: The combination of two ammonium transport activity sensors from different organisms will be useful for dissecting endogenous control mechanisms, because heterologous proteins are not expected to be subject to the same regulatory control and can thus serve as references.
evidence: This is a speculation about future applications of the sensors.

claim: Heterologous proteins are not expected to be subject to the same regulatory control and can thus serve as references.
source: The combination of two ammonium transport activity sensors from different organisms will be useful for dissecting endogenous control mechanisms, because heterologous proteins are not expected to be subject to the same regulatory control and can thus serve as references.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about heterologous expression systems.
